query:
The family has a norm that everyone comes home for Christmas. Does this apply to all family members?

Options:
A. Dad
B. Imogen
C. Kofi
D. Mum
context:
[1] (about=Mum, episodic, t5 @2025-07-28T18:02:00) Right, Christmas! Everyone home, yes? I'll do the full works. Kofi, booked your flights? 🎄🙏
[2] (about=Mum, episodic, t6 @2025-07-28T22:58:00) Oh Kofi 😭😭😭 but we said everyone. It won't be the same without you. Are you sure?
[3] (about=Dad, episodic, t6 @2025-07-28T23:25:00) Don't build Christmas around airline pricing. We'll cope. Dad.
[4] (about=Imogen, episodic, t6 @2025-07-28T23:04:00) Mum let him figure it out, flights are genuinely a lot. Kofi we'll do a video call Christmas morning either way 💙
[5] (about=Kofi, episodic, t8 @2025-08-04T23:22:00) I know. I know. Maybe not Christmas every year but I do want an extra visit if I can swing it.
[6] (about=GROUP, said_by=Mum, group-interaction, t6 @2025-07-28T22:51:00) Flexible on Christmas lunch timing or Boxing Day to include Kofi
agent_answer:
Yes — Mum states the norm as “everyone home,” and she reminds Kofi “we said everyone.” So the norm applies to all four family members:

- **Dad** – included in the norm; he is home and says they’ll cope without reshaping Christmas around Kofi’s flights.
- **Imogen** – included; she will be home and plans a video call with Kofi.
- **Kofi** – included in the norm, but he is the one not coming this year (“Maybe not Christmas every year…”).
- **Mum** – included; she is hosting and trying to adjust timing to include Kofi.

So the norm applies to all family members, with Kofi being the current exception.
